topic: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max): what the index result really is, and which machine runs the weights
thesis: DeepSeek's Flash 1017 is the first front-page drop that is both a top-of-class open-weight reasoning model and a same-day local download, but at 552B backbone parameters plus an Engram memory the machine that runs it is a 128 GB unified-memory box, not a gaming card.
explanation_path: Establish what the name is before any scoreboard: 1017 is an upgrade of the existing V4.1 Flash, shipped 2026-10-17, same weights family, and Max is the top of a reasoning-effort dial on one set of weights, not a second model. With that anchor, the index result lands honestly: 45 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, second of 121 among open-weight large reasoning models, six points over its predecessor, with closed models still above it overall. Then the size reality, because Flash misleads: the architecture is a 552B-parameter backbone with a 196B-parameter Engram lookup memory, activating only 16B parameters per token during decode, which is why it is cheap on the API yet heavy on disk. The payoff is the local question already answered: weights are MIT and downloadable today, a community quant is sized for exactly one 128 GB DGX Spark, the llama.cpp route still needs two 96 GB cards plus host RAM and an unmerged PR, and a single 24 GB GeForce is not in this model's future at any quant. What a gaming-card viewer takes away is the API price and the knowledge of which machine class to watch.

claims.claim: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash-1017 on 2026-10-17 as an upgrade of V4.1 Flash, live on web, app and API the same day.
The 1017 weights are open on Hugging Face under the MIT License (Safetensors, 48 shards), with the card listing a model size of 763B params.

The architecture is a mixture-of-experts model with a 552B backbone plus a 196B Engram conditional memory, activating 8B parameters per token in prefill and 16B during decode, with a 1M-token context.

Max is not a separate model: the official card exposes a continuously controllable reasoning-effort setting from 1 to 100, and Artificial Analysis lists (Max) as that effort level on the same weights.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (Max) scores 45 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ranking #2 of 121 in its open-weight class.
It does not top the overall index: AA's comparison list shows Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback), Claude Sonnet 5.5, Muse Wonder Full, GPT-6 Astra and others ranked above it.
claims.source_title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page and comparison list

claims.claim: The API lists at $0.30 per 1M input tokens and $1.20 per 1M output tokens, and AA measures cost per Intelligence Index task at $0.26, down from the predecessor's $0.49.

In DeepSeek's own benchmarks relayed by The Decoder, 1017 beats larger models including Claude Opus 5, GPT 5.6-Sol, Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 in several coding and agent categories, hitting DeepSWE v1.1 77.0 percent at just under $0.20 per task versus the predecessor's 74.2 percent at around $0.50.
claims.source_title: The Decoder: DeepSeek's smaller model beats larger rivals in agentic tasks

claims.claim: A community VQ GGUF conversion finished and uploaded the same day (2026-10-17): a 113,556,639,424-byte base GGUF (about 106 GiB resident, --mem-budget-mb 110000) explicitly sized for one 128 GB DGX Spark, loadable only by the ds4-dfm-rs runtime.

The llama.cpp route is a 261.4 GiB IQ2_XS build targeting two 96 GB GPUs (roughly 79 GiB per card) plus about 115 GiB of host RAM for the Engram tables, and it requires an unmerged llama.cpp branch (PR #28696), marked experimental.
On the independent Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Max, Default Fallback) holds the highest score at 63.6%.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: a library where every question wakes only six of 384 shelves
analogy_candidates.mapping: the 552B backbone is the shelves of books, the 196B Engram tables are the card catalog consulted before any shelf opens, and the 16B active parameters are the few shelves actually read per token, which is why it thinks like a giant but bills like a small model
analogy_candidates.limit: the catalog is nearly half the weight of the books and must ride in RAM or on disk no matter which shelves you open, so the building cannot shrink below the catalog

analogy_candidates.mapping: Max is the temperature dial on the same 1017 oven, one set of weights with a reasoning-effort setting from 1 to 100 that sets how long it thinks before answering
analogy_candidates.limit: a hotter oven costs real time and tokens, and AA still ranks the model among the most verbose (210M output tokens on the index run)

misconceptions.myth: DeepSeek 1017 (Max) is now the top AI model overall
misconceptions.reality: 45 is #2 of 121 among open-weight large reasoning models on AA v4.3.2, with Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra above it overall (claims 5, 6)

misconceptions.myth: No local weights yet, Flash 1017 is API-only
misconceptions.reality: MIT weights shipped on Hugging Face the same day, and a community quant is already sized for a 128 GB DGX Spark (claims 2, 9)

misconceptions.myth: It is called Flash, so it fits a gaming card
misconceptions.reality: 552B backbone plus about 196B Engram tables means even 2-bit builds target 128 GB unified memory or two 96 GB cards (claims 3, 9, 10)

glossary.definition: a model architecture that stores many specialist sub-networks (experts) and activates only a few per token
the subset of a model's weights actually used to process one token, the number that drives speed and cost
DeepSeek's lookup-table memory (196B parameters in this architecture) consulted via token-based lookup before the main network runs
the single-file weight format used by llama.cpp and friends for running models locally
shrinking weight precision (for example 4-bit) to cut file size and memory at some accuracy cost
a dial for how long a model thinks before answering; on 1017 it is an integer from 1 to 100, and Max is its top
an independent aggregate score (v4.3.2, ten evaluations) comparing models across reasoning and agent tasks
a machine design where CPU and GPU share one memory pool, such as the DGX Spark's 128 GB

unverified: 1017 (Max) as a distinct DeepSeek product: no fetched official page names one; officially, Max is the top of a 1-100 reasoning-effort dial.
The exact total size of the official safetensors checkpoint: a community page reports a 510 GB official checkpoint, but no fetched official page states a total.
Performance on the channel's own DGX Spark (tokens per second, load time): not measured; a first-party number should replace this line.
A Hacker News discussion title suggesting 24 GB of VRAM plus disk streaming is enough for 1017: the discussion page was not fetched.
Stock-llama.cpp GGUFs of 1017 (for example mrfakename or unsloth repos): seen only as search snippets; llama.cpp support rides the unmerged PR #28696.
The radar's 152 points / 54 comments thread was not found; the fetched HN thread (item 50129045) shows 941 points and 706 comments.
suggested_outline:
Hook on the correction: 1017 (Max) just scored 45 on the Artificial Analysis index, number two of 121 open-weight models, and the weights are already downloadable, not when GGUFs.
What actually shipped on 2026-10-17: MIT weights, a 552B-parameter backbone with an Engram lookup memory, only 16B active per token, 1M context; Max is the effort dial, not a bigger model.
The local fit answered: a community quant already sized for one 128 GB DGX Spark (about 106 GiB resident); the llama.cpp route still wants two 96 GB cards plus host RAM and an unmerged PR; a 24 GB gaming card is out, and the cheap API ($0.26 per index task) is the gaming-card viewer's takeaway.
notes: Conflict: The Decoder's beats-larger-models line relays DeepSeek's own benchmark charts (per-benchmark margins live in images), and it noted independent benchmarks had not come out yet at publish; AA's measured speed is slightly down (227.1 vs 231.2 output tokens per second) even as cost per task halved, and independent Terminal-Bench 4.0 is led by Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Max) at 63.6%. The Decoder names GPT 5.6-Sol where AA now lists GPT-6.1 Sol, likely a rename between article and leaderboard. Tier note: the community quant sizes (claims 9, 10) are community-tier, so the narration should attribute them (the converter reports about 106 GiB); key numbers are all primary- or benchmark-backed. The radar's tops-the-index premise is corrected by claims 5 and 6; keep the reframe, drop the global crown.
viewer_situation: You have watched every DeepSeek open drop run on local hardware, and you have one 24 GB gaming card waiting for the next one.
objection: It is 763B parameters on the card, so Flash is marketing, nothing consumer-sized runs it without a 128 GB unified-memory box or two workstation cards, and the index crown is only within open weights.
